module.purpose: Provides CSS parsing utilities for extracting imports, font-face declarations, font families, and external URLs used by the editor export pipeline.
module.summary: This module uses regular expressions to identify CSS imports, @font-face blocks, font-family values, and url() references. It resolves font URLs against a base URL, excludes fragment-only references, normalizes font-family names to lowercase, and filters CSS properties that should not be included in exported styling. Parsing is synchronous and returns arrays or sets without mutating caller inputs.
module.businessContext: Supports exporting editor content with usable CSS resources and font metadata. Failures can omit imports, fonts, or relevant styling from exported documents.
classes: ParsedFontFace (~L3-7): Represents parsed font-face CSS, resolved URLs, and normalized family names
functions: parseCssImports (~L36-38): Extracts imported stylesheet URLs and trailing import options
parseCssFontFaces (~L40-53): Parses font-face blocks and resolves embedded resource URLs
parseCssFontFamilyValue (~L55-82): Splits and normalizes comma-separated font-family values
shouldIncludeCssProperty (~L84-94): Determines whether a CSS property belongs in exported styles
parseCss (~L96-100): Combines stylesheet import and font-face parsing results
parseCssValueUrls (~L102-107): Extracts non-fragment URLs from a CSS value

moduleContractTests.scenario: An import declaration contains a quoted URL and trailing media or feature text.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Pins extraction of both the imported resource and text following the URL.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A font-face declaration contains a relative font URL and a quoted family name.
given: const css = '@font-face { font-family: "Open Sans"; src: url("fonts/open.woff2"); }'
moduleContractTests.then: returns one face with fontFamilies equal to new Set(['open sans']), urls[0].original equal to 'fonts/open.woff2', and urls[0].resolved equal to 'https://example.com/css/fonts/open.woff2'
moduleContractTests.rationale: Guards URL resolution and case normalization in the parsed font-face contract.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A font-family value mixes quoted and unquoted family names separated by commas.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Pins supported quoting, separator handling, and lowercase normalization.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A property is vendor-prefixed, animation-related, or explicitly excluded.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Preserves the complete exclusion policy for properties that should not be included.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A normal CSS property does not match any exclusion rule.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Ensures filtering is allow-by-default outside the explicit exclusions.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A CSS value contains an external URL and a fragment-only URL.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Pins exclusion of in-document fragment references while retaining external resources.

moduleContractTests.scenario: CSS contains both an import declaration and a font-face declaration.
given: const css = '@import url("base.css"); @font-face { font-family: serif; src: url(font.woff2); }'
moduleContractTests.then: returns an object whose imports has one parsed import and whose fontFaces has one parsed font face
moduleContractTests.rationale: Guards the aggregate parser contract and delegation to both CSS parsers.

units.name: parseCssImports

detail.name: parseCssImports
detail.returnType: Array<{ url: string | undefined; extras: string | undefined }>
preconditions: The import-matching regular expression is available to the function.
postconditions: Returns one record for each match produced by the import-matching regular expression, in match order.
Each record has a url property selected from captures 1 through 5 using first-truthy fallback semantics.
Each record has an extras property equal to capture 6.
invariants: The result preserves the order of matches.
The result length equals the number of matches produced by the regular expression.
No input or matched capture is mutated.
edgeCases: When an earlier URL capture is an empty or otherwise falsy string, the next capture is selected.
When all URL captures 1 through 5 are falsy or absent, url is undefined.
When capture 6 is absent, extras is undefined.
When there are no matches, an empty array is returned.

raises: Any error raised by css.matchAll or Array.from propagates to the caller.

detail.ioFormatSpec: Returns an array of objects with exactly the fields { url, extras }, where url is m[1] || m[2] || m[3] || m[4] || m[5] and extras is m[6].
detail.summary: Parses CSS import matches into an ordered array of import records, selecting the first truthy captured URL and preserving the sixth capture as extras.

units.name: parseCssFontFaces

detail.name: parseCssFontFaces
detail.signature: export function parseCssFontFaces(css: string, baseUrl: string)
preconditions: css is a string containing zero or more CSS font-face declarations.
baseUrl is a string usable as the base for URL resolution.
postconditions: Returns one ParsedFontFace result for each font-face declaration matched in css.
Each discovered font URL preserves its original URL text.
Each discovered font URL has a resolved href or null when safe URL resolution fails.
Discovered font family names are normalized to lowercase and deduplicated within each font-face result.
invariants: Font-face results preserve the order of matches in css.
URL results preserve the order of URL matches within each font-face declaration.
Font family values are represented uniquely per font-face declaration.
edgeCases: CSS containing no matching font-face declarations returns an empty array.
A font-face declaration with no matching URLs produces an empty URL collection.
A font-face declaration with no matching font-family values produces an empty font-family collection.
An URL that cannot be safely resolved against baseUrl produces a null resolved value while retaining its original value.
Font-family values differing only by letter case are normalized to the same lowercase value and deduplicated.

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: No explicit validation or exception conversion is specified; URL resolution failures are converted to a null resolved URL.
errorPolicy.returnsOnError: Returns an empty result for CSS with no matching font-face declarations; individual unresolvable URLs retain their original value with resolved set to null.

detail.ioFormatSpec: Returns an array of ParsedFontFace objects. Each font-face object contains URL entries with original and resolved fields, and a deduplicated lowercase collection of font-family values.
detail.summary: Parses CSS font-face declarations and returns their discovered font families and source URLs. Each URL includes its original text and a safely resolved absolute URL when resolution succeeds.

specTests.then: The returned array has one result per declaration in source order; URL matches retain their order, and font-family values are lowercase and deduplicated.
The corresponding URL entry retains its original value and has resolved equal to null.

units.name: parseCssFontFamilyValue

detail.name: parseCssFontFamilyValue
preconditions: value is a string containing a CSS font-family value or text to parse
postconditions: Returns a Set<string> containing each successfully parsed font family name in lowercase
Duplicate font family names collapse to one set entry
invariants: All returned font family names are lowercase
The result contains no duplicate values
edgeCases: An empty string produces an empty set
A comma-separated list is parsed into separate font family entries
Single-quoted and double-quoted family names are accepted without their surrounding quotes
Unquoted family names are accepted when they contain no semicolon, newline, whitespace, comma, or quote
Names differing only by letter case produce one lowercase set entry

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: No explicit validation error is raised; values that do not match the parsing expressions are omitted or result in an empty set.
errorPolicy.returnsOnError: A Set containing only successfully matched and normalized font family names.

detail.summary: Parses a CSS font-family value into a set of normalized family names. Quoted and unquoted family values are recognized from a comma-separated list and normalized to lowercase.

specLiterals.role: Recognizes unquoted, double-quoted, and single-quoted CSS font family values.
Recognizes comma separators between CSS font family values.

specTests.when: parseCssFontFamilyValue is called with that input.
specTests.then: The result is a set containing exactly "arial", "helvetica neue", and "sans-serif".
The result is an empty Set.

units.name: shouldIncludeCssProperty

detail.name: shouldIncludeCssProperty
postconditions: Returns false for vendor-prefixed properties, properties beginning with animation, properties beginning with transition, cursor, and pointer-events.
Returns true for other CSS property names.
invariants: The input property string is not modified.
edgeCases: An empty property string is not excluded by any filter and returns true.
A property beginning with '-' returns false.
A property beginning with 'animation' returns false.
A property beginning with 'transition' returns false.
The exact properties 'cursor' and 'pointer-events' return false.
Other property names return true.
